rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-3 (substitutability): some packaging users can reduce their use of taxed plastic at a cost below 200 T a tonne.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-2 (substitutability): imported empty packaging is at the margin of supply and foreign converters absorb little, so packaging users bear more of the tax than sellers do.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-2 (substitutability), the premise of C-56 and C-64: part of the tax stays with sellers: converters' after-tax price falls (C-56, with A-20) and foreign converters' price before tax falls (C-64).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-11 (substitutability): packaging is a material part of the cost of some packaged goods (6% to 10% for bottled water and pre-packed produce) and their sellers cannot switch fully at the old cost.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-24 (revenue_use): the plastics unit is funded by the 7 million T appropriation in the Act, from the general budget that receives the tax.
evidence: The Act appropriates 7 million T a year from the general budget for the plastics unit.

rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-16 (expectations): liable firms can store packaging and bring orders forward into late 2027.
evidence: The tax was announced in the budget statement of 2 March 2027, enacted on 28 June 2027 and takes effect on 1 January 2028.

rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-062 (illustrative figures), A-32 (substitutability): some plastic components can be redesigned so that another material is the heaviest by weight, at a cost below the tax saved (A-4: raising recycled content to 30% costs less than the tax for some components, p 0.85, is the second route out of the definition); I take the lower row, since C-5 cites both.
evidence: "A plastic packaging component containing 30 per cent or more recycled plastic is not chargeable."
